title: security-compliance-review-prep-1on1-draft
content:
Context: 1:1 with Maya (manager, sec & compliance) to align on upcoming SOC2 readiness review and ISO scoping. Quick notes and ask list so I can leave the meeting with clear next steps.

Meeting goals:
- Confirm scope for SOC2 readiness run (services, hosted API, dedicated control plane, private deploy options).
- Validate evidence map gaps and owners.
- Prioritize vendor risk items that need remediation before auditor kickoff.
- Agree next checkpoints and who owns auditor Q&A.

High-level status (my view):
- SOC2: control mapping done for core infra and API; documentation patchy for private deployments and customer-managed KMS integration. Some control owners assigned, but several controls still unassigned (change mgmt, vendor management).
- ISO: scoping discussion pending (do we include private on-prem customers in scope? likely out-of-scope unless we host their data).
- Vendor risk: vendor inventory exists but not all contracts have updated security addenda; no formal risk scoring tied to SLAs.

Evidence / gaps I expect auditors to ask for:
- SOC2: evidence of access reviews (last 12 months), change control tickets for infra changes, incident response postmortems with timeline to resolution, encryption key management docs + KMS integration diagrams for private deployments.
- ISO: asset inventory, risk assessment, statement of applicability (SoA) draft.
- Vendor: updated vendor risk register, signed DPA/SAAs for top-10 vendors, recent vendor penetration test results where applicable.

Quick ask list for Maya (questions to cover in 1:1):
1) Confirm final SOC2 scope and whether Dedicated and Private are included as in-scope systems. If private is partially in-scope, what boundary language do we want for customer-managed infra?
2) Who owns vendor risk remediation? Is it central SecOps or product (owner per vendor)? I need an assigned owner for the top-10 vendors by criticality.
3) Evidence centralization: can we push auditors to the Drive folder + Confluence evidence map, or do they insist on an external portal? Any preference?
4) Approval for additional headcount/contractor to help collect historical evidence (change logs, ticket exports) — estimate 2–3 weeks of effort.
5) Risk appetite: are there any controls we deem acceptable to defer to next cycle (low-severity items)? Want a list of items to present to auditors as 'deferred with compensating controls'.

Immediate action items (draft for meeting agreement):
- Aaron: produce a prioritized evidence gap spreadsheet (assign owners column) by EOD Thu.
- Maya: confirm SOC2 scope and send note with scope statement and any high-level exclusions by Mon.
- Priya: pull last 12 months of access review exports and share link to Drive folder by Fri.
- Engineering (cc: infra leads): provide list of change tickets for last 6 months labeled "production infra"; target next Tue.
- Legal: confirm status of DPAs with top-10 vendors and provide copy of any pending SAAs; target next Wed.

Notes on vendor risk (quick thoughts):
- Top concerns: cloud infra provider (region compliance), KMS/HSM provider for private deployments, observability vendor (logs retention), and third-party auth (SSO) provider.
- Short-term mitigation: require updated security addenda before auditor kickoff for any vendor that stores customer data.
- Medium-term: implement vendor scoring in the console (exposure + data sensitivity) so product teams can see impact.

Evidence map gaps I already identified (examples):
- Change management: need ticket links for 4 major infra changes (Nov-Feb) + approval records.
- Access reviews: one-off reviews exist but not consolidated; need a single report showing reviewer + outcome.
- KMS: architecture diagram exists but missing cloud-config screenshots and rotation policy doc.
- Incident response: need timeline artifacts for two incidents (Q1) showing detection->mitigation->remediation.

Potential blockers I want Maya to help unblock:
- Pulling historical tickets (requires infra lead time and export creds) — may need temporary SRE contractor.
- Legal sign-off on DPAs — possible delay if vendors request negotiations.
- Deciding ISO scope — needs exec alignment if we expand scope.

Suggested timeline (internal):
- Week 0 (this week): finalize SOC2 scope, owner assignments, evidence gap spreadsheet.
- Week 1–2: collect evidence for high-priority controls, legal to chase DPAs.
- Week 3: internal dry-run with auditors (tabletop) and finalize evidence portal.
- Week 4: auditor kickoff.

Prep notes for the 1:1 (things I'm going to say):
- "We have a lot of the mapping done, but pulling historic evidence is the real time sink. I'm asking for 2–3 weeks of focused help to get us ready."
- "We should be explicit about private deployment boundaries — I don't want auditors expecting us to show proofs for customer-managed on-prem installs."
- "Vendor risk needs clearer ownership — I'll draft a proposal to centralize remediation tracking if you want me to."

Follow-ups to capture in meeting:
- Maya to confirm scope and scope note text.
- Agreement on who chases DPAs and timeline.
- Resource approval (contractor or reallocation) for ticket/evidence collection.

Misc quick links I might reference in the meeting:
- Confluence: SOC2 Evidence Map (linked above)
- Drive: evidence folder (linked above)
- Jira: JIRA-1234 (vendor risk epic)

Open questions for later:
- Do we want to run a limited internal SOC2 SOC readiness engagement (external consultant)? Pros/cons and budget.
- Should ISO scoping include Dedicated pools in EU only to start?

-- end of notes --

(keeping this as my working doc — will move to shared Confluence once we align on owners and timeline)
